tasks.title: p-timeout clear() should report whether it cleared an active timeout
tasks.prompt: In the real p-timeout codebase, the clear() method currently clears the timeout but does not report whether it actually cleared an active timer. Update clear() so it returns true when it clears a currently active timeout and false when the timer has already been cleared, the wrapped promise has already settled, or the timeout already fired. Preserve existing timeout, fallback, abort, custom timer, and listener cleanup behavior. Add focused runtime coverage in test.js and type coverage in index.test-d.ts, and update the public ClearablePromise type in index.d.ts. Keep the change scoped to index.js, test.js, index.d.ts, and index.test-d.ts only. Do not modify package metadata, dependency files, readme, or docs. Run the verifier before finishing, using the verifier command exactly as provided.

anti_shortcut_rules: Do not modify package metadata, package-lock.json, dependency files, readme, or documentation for this task.
Update runtime behavior in index.js, runtime tests in test.js, public ClearablePromise type in index.d.ts, and type assertion in index.test-d.ts.
clear() must return true only when it clears an active timeout token, and false after clear() has already been called, after the wrapped promise settles, or after the timeout fires.
Preserve abort listener cleanup, custom timer call style, fallback behavior, message:false behavior, and cancelable promise behavior.
Name runtime tests with verifier-visible wording such as `clear() returns`, `clear return`, `clear state`, or `active timeout`.
In test.js include direct assertions where `.clear()` returns both true and false.
Do not claim success until npm test passes through the provided verifier.
